title: Res sends E_Φ to E_M (Prop 8.1)
body_html:
$\Res$ preserves homological isomorphisms

Let $E_\Phi$ (resp. $E_M$) be the class of morphisms in $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ (resp. $\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M))$) that induce an isomorphism after $H_0$.

Proposition (Sheaf7 Prop 8.1). $\Res(E_\Phi) \subseteq E_M$ and $\Sat(E_M) \subseteq E_\Phi$.
proof_html:
outline

Given $s : \mathscr{V}_1 \to \mathscr{V}_2$ in $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$. Set $\mathscr{W}_i := \Res \mathscr{V}_i$. Since taking $K_{x,0+}$- and $M_{x, 0+}$-coinvariants is exact, the isomorphism $i_x$ of i_x: C_d(B(Σ),𝒱)_x ≅ C_d(B(M),𝒲)_x gives the commutative diagram (for each $\mathscr{V}_i$): $$(\kappa_x^* \otimes H_0(C_\bullet \BSigma, \mathscr{V}_i))_{K_{x,0+}} \cong H_0((\kappa_x^* \otimes C_\bullet \BSigma, \mathscr{V}_i)_{K_{x,0+}}) \cong H_0(C_\bullet(\mathcal{B}(M), \mathscr{W}_i)_{M_{x, 0+}}) \cong H_0(C_\bullet(\mathcal{B}(M), \mathscr{W}_i))_{M_{x, 0+}}.$$

Now $H_0(s)$ is an iso in $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ iff $\Hom_{K_{x,0+}}(\kappa_x, H_0(s))$ is iso for every vertex $x$ of $\mathcal{B}(M)$. Similarly $H_0(\Res s)$ is iso iff $H_0(\Res s)^{M_{x, 0+}}$ is iso for every vertex. The diagram above shows the two conditions agree. $\square$

This is the single most important statement in §8: it is the bridge that lets the §7.4 localization equivalence on $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ match the analogous one on $\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M))$ for depth-zero $M$.
